item.title: Atiku to Tinubu: 2027 conversation is how to repair damage your govt caused
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has told President Bola Tinubu that his administration’s failures will cost him re-election in 2027, challenging him to defend his record in office rather than attack his investment in education. Read Also: * Hunger: Tinubu tackles Atiku, asks how he built university as VP * Any Nigerian that’s not lazy will have food on the table – Yari Atiku, the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, said Nigerians had endured enough hardship under Tinubu’s leadership, insisting that the next presidential election would be about reversing the damage “inflicted on the country through rising poverty, insecurity, unemployment and a crushing cost-of-living crisis”. In a statement on Saturday by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, Atiku also defended his investment in the American University of Nigeria, AUN, insisting that his educational venture began before he became Vice President in 1999. “The answer is simple: my investment in education predates my time in public service. “In 1993, I was laying the foundation for ABTI Academy. That Academy has since grown into the American University of Nigeria,” Atiku said. He accused Tinubu of attempting to undermine his record in education because he could account for his own business and political journey. Turning to the economy, the former Vice President said Tinubu had no business seeking another mandate when millions of Nigerians were struggling with the consequences of his policies. “A president who has plunged the country into a crushing cost-of-living crisis has no business asking Nigerians for another mandate. The real conversation about the 2027 election is how to repair the damage your government has done,” Atiku said. He also challenged the President’s insistence that Nigeria could not return to fuel subsidy, questioning the benefits of the economic reforms to ordinary Nigerians. “You say Nigeria cannot return to subsidy and must move forward. But you cannot even tell Nigerians where you are taking them. Forward into deeper poverty, mounting debt, insecurity and mass unemployment?” he asked. Atiku accused the administration of creating widespread poverty and being insensitive to the plight of struggling Nigerians, citing a reported comment by Tinubu’s campaign Director-General that hungry Nigerians were lazy. “You created poverty, then insult the people suffering from it. You attack my Affordable Life campaign, but the people you are really attacking are the millions of Nigerians desperate for relief from your failed leadership,” he said. item.title: Breaking: Nigeria’s Flamingos beat Japan 2-1 to win first U-17 Women’s World Cup
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde Nigeria’s U-17 women’s national team, the Flamingos, have defeated Japan 2-1 to win the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco. The Flamingos secured the historic victory on Saturday at the Mohammed VI Football Complex, Pitch 3, in Rabat, to claim their first title in the competition. Awawu Bashiru opened the scoring for Nigeria in the 39th minute with a long-range effort that slipped through the hands of the Japanese goalkeeper. Nigeria doubled their advantage shortly after the restart, with Oluebube Umejiaku finding the net in the 47th minute to put the Flamingos in control. Japan fought back and reduced the deficit through Fuki Ito in the 80th minute. The Japanese side pushed for an equaliser, but Nigeria held on to secure the 2-1 victory. The Flamingos also came close to extending their lead late in the game, striking the crossbar from a corner kick. item.title: Arsenal Edge Hull To Extend Premier League Lead As Tottenham Lose To Leeds
item.description: Arsenal beat stubborn Hull 1-0 to stretch their lead at the top of the Premier League to six points on Saturday while Tottenham’s recent revival was halted by Leeds. Mikel Arteta’s Gunners were strongly tipped to get the better of the visitors, who have not won in the league since August, but were made to sweat despite dominating the match. Captain Martin Odegaard finally broke the deadlock for the champions and title favourites in the 72nd minute to give Arsenal their ninth win in 10 league games. Arsenal, who bossed possession at the Emirates, had a claim for a penalty in the closing minutes of the first half after Kai Havertz had his shirt pulled by Nobel Mendy. But VAR ruled that the German forward was in an offside position in the build-up. Arsenal’s Norwegian midfielder #08 Martin Odegaard celebrates scoring the team’s first goal during the English Premier League football match between Arsenal and Hull City at the Emirates Stadium in London on November 7, 2026. (Photo by Henry Nicholls / AFP) Frustration mounted as the second half unfolded but Odegaard came to Arsenal’s rescue, scoring his first goal since early September with a poacher’s finish. Noni Madueke cut in from the right before unleashing a left-footed shot that Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis spilled and Odegaard fired home from close range. Arsenal manager Arteta said he was happy with the performance but wanted his team to be more clinical after they recorded a third 1-0 win in four league games. “I think it is time to praise my players. What they have done not only today but after the international break is remarkable because of the games,” he told the BBC. He added: “We have some great moments, we need to put the chances we are creating against the opponent into the scoreline. That is what we need to improve.” Arsenal’s English midfielder #41 Declan Rice reacts after failing to score during the English Premier League football match between Arsenal and Hull City at the Emirates Stadium in London on November 7, 2026. (Photo by Henry Nicholls / AFP) VAR controversy In the early kick-off, Leeds struck in the 79th minute through substitute Noah Okafor to end Tottenham’s three-match winning run. The major talking point in the first half was a challenge by Leeds defender Jayden Bogle on Spurs winger Mathys Tel, which was reviewed for a potential red card by VAR officials before eventually being cleared. Tel had to leave the field shortly before half-time. Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi, disappointed by his team’s second-half showing, refused to be drawn on the incident, which was not reviewed on the pitchside monitor by referee John Brooks. “In the first situation of Mathys Tel I didn’t see, I can’t say nothing,” he told TNT Sports after the 1-0 defeat. item.title: EPL: Delap double condemns Man City to third straight defeat
item.description: Manchester City slumped to a third consecutive Premier League defeat on Saturday as Liam Delap’s double lifted Nottingham Forest out of the relegation zone with a 3-1 win at the City Ground. Oliver Glasner’s men had not scored at home at all this season, but pounced on City’s defensive errors to strike twice in the first 20 minutes through Jair Cunha and Delap. Rayan Cherki’s stunning strike gave City hope, but their title challenge is rapidly wilting even before the potential effects of a major points deduction. Delap sealed just Forest’s second win of the season with an incredible strike in off the post on the night that could launch his career for the two-time European champions, after a difficult start since his club-record £50 million ($67 million) move from Chelsea. Defeat leaves City six points adrift of leaders Arsenal and with questions over whether the uncertainty surrounding the club is playing a part in their on-field slump. Found guilty on over 100 Premier League charges of breaking financial rules, the 10-time English champions face a severe points penalty unless they can overturn that verdict on appeal. Glasner warned his players he would make big changes after a disappointing start to his reign saw them start the match in the bottom three. The Austrian got the response he craved as Forest burst out of the blocks to pounce on City’s sloppiness at the back. – Clinical Forest – Cunha robbed Josko Gvardiol midway inside the City half and was allowed to bear down on goal before slotting past Gianluigi Donnarumma. Forest’s first home goal in 511 minutes was celebrated wildly at the City Ground with owner Evangelos Marinakis jumping out of his chair in celebration. Elliott Anderson had a night to forget on his first return to Forest since a reported £116 million move to City. Xaver Schlager beat Anderson to the ball in midfield and set Delap running from inside his own half before unleashing an unstoppable drive past Donnarumma for his first home goal for the club. However, he has been hit with the task of trying to keep his players motivated when they do not know if they will even be in the English top-flight next season. Maresca showed his frustration with a double change at half-time with the introduction of Nico O’Reilly and Matheus Nunes helping to spark a brief City rally. Cherki smashed home a sweet strike from Jeremy Doku’s deflected cross to halve the arrears. Erling Haaland then nearly levelled when the Norwegian flashed a shot just wide. City, though, remained vulnerable to the Forest counter-attack and were picked off again for the decisive goal 15 minutes from time. item.title: ‘Huge dream’ to play for England with Jude – Jobe Bellingham
item.description: Borussia Dortmund midfielder Jobe Bellingham said Saturday he hoped to fulfil a “huge dream” by playing alongside brother Jude after being called up to the England squad. On Friday, England manager Thomas Tuchel named Jobe, 21, in England’s 25-man squad for November’s Nations League fixtures with Croatia and Spain. Speaking after Dortmund’s 2-1 home win over Elversberg in the Bundesliga, Jobe said he and brother had acted out playing together for England when they were kids. “It’s really good. I don’t want to get too carried away, but it’s obviously a big dream for me and for Jude as well,” the younger Bellingham told DAZN. “Since we were young, we reenacted that so many times in the garden or wherever, in the park, playing for England together. “So it’s a huge dream. It’s not happened yet, so I don’t want to jinx or say it too early, but yeah, I’m really excited.” Jobe has captained England’s under-21s but this is his first senior call-up. Real Madrid midfielder Jude, 23, who also made his England debut while playing for Dortmund, now has 60 England caps. Jobe took time to adapt to the Bundesliga since joining in 2025 but has impressed this season and has become an established member of Dortmund’s starting XI. Speaking on Friday, Dortmund coach Niko Kovac praised Jobe’s development and dedication to improving his game. “He is really a complete football freak. He studies his own game and the games of other players to learn from the best in his position. “And he’s a really great lad and he’s got an excellent attitude. I’m really happy for him that he can now wear the jersey of his national team next to his brother. “It’s something quite special, not just to play for your country, but to play alongside your brother. It’s incredible.” Vanguard News The post ‘Huge dream’ to play for England with Jude – Jobe Bellingham appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.description: By Olayinka Latona The General Overseer of the Redeemed Christian Church of God, RCCG, Pastor Enoch Adejare Adeboye, ordered the return of billions of Naira traced to church projects from an individual under investigation for alleged financial crimes within 24 hours, the Chairman of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission, EFCC, Ola Olukoyede, has said. Olukoyede said Adeboye gave the directive immediately after the commission briefed him on the investigation and the discovery that proceeds of the alleged financial crimes had been traced to some RCCG projects. The EFCC chairman disclosed this while addressing church workers and ministers after the monthly Holy Ghost Service at the Redemption City of God, Simawa, Ogun State. The programme, held at the invitation of Adeboye, had as its theme, “Ethical Standard and Corruption in Christian Community.” Recounting the incident, Olukoyede said the individual under investigation was involved in financial transactions worth tens of billions of naira, some of which the commission traced to the church. He said he personally approached Adeboye to explain the findings, adding that the cleric reacted angrily and immediately directed church officials to return the funds. “The reaction on the face of Daddy was like I was almost blaming myself for taking the matter to him. Daddy was visibly angry. He called one or two pastors and said, ‘I give you 24 hours. Everything you have traced to RCCG from this particular person who has been indicted, return it within the next 24 hours’. “That money was returned to the coffers of government. That is what RCCG is known for. That is who we are. We are not the custodian of proceeds of crime,” he said. Olukoyede, who is also a senior pastor in the RCCG, made the disclosure while addressing church workers and ministers after the monthly Holy Ghost Service at the Redemption City of God, Simawa, Ogun State. It was a day that I had calls to detain a very senior pastor in this mission. I had no choice. item.title: ‘Collect Their Money, Spend It, But Vote Your Heart’, Makinde Tells Supporters
item.description: The presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde, has urged his supporters to accept money offered by politicians but vote according to their conscience. Makinde gave the advice on Saturday at his presidential campaign rally in Bauchi State, where he told supporters not to feel guilty about collecting such money while remaining loyal to their preferred candidate. “Don’t bother at all. When they bring money, it is your money, collect it, but vote your heart and I know your heart is with us and APM,” he said. ﻿ The Oyo governor pledged to reset Nigeria’s economy, security architecture and socio-political environment if elected president. He said Nigerians unhappy with the state of the country should support his “Reset Nigeria” agenda. “If you are not happy with the way things are in our country today, if you are not happy that there is no enough inclusivity, if you are not happy that your government cannot tell you the truth, they cannot handle our issues with sincerity, then there is only one part for us and the part is to reset Nigeria. So, I am asking you today to be a resetter,” Makinde said. Also addressing the rally, the party’s vice-presidential candidate, Lawal Daura, said the politics of lies, deceit and hypocrisy was threatening democracy in Nigeria. He said the APM’s reset agenda was designed to tackle these challenges and ensure that anyone elected into government would be committed to honesty and sincerity. The party’s national leader and Bauchi State Governor, Bala Mohammed, said the APM’s agenda had solutions to Nigeria’s problems. Mohammed said he was supporting Makinde’s presidential ambition because the governor had demonstrated that he was hardworking and committed to carrying everyone along. The rally drew party supporters dressed in outfits bearing the APM colours, as well as party leaders, including its national chairman. item.title: Delta Political Tension: Injuries, destruction as another Obi-Kwankwaso rally comes under attack
item.description: NDC fingers APC over attacks Baseless allegation with no proof — APC By Egufe Yafugborhi ASABA — Political tension heightened in Delta State on Saturday as supporters of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), backing the presidential ambition of Peter Obi and Rabiu Kwankwaso, came under attack during a one-million-man march in Asaba, leaving several persons injured and campaign vehicles vandalised. The incident, which came after a similar disruption of the movement’s rally in Effurun, Delta State, reportedly involved suspected thugs armed with sticks, knives, machetes and other dangerous weapons. The vehicles, many branded with campaign banners bearing the images of Obi, his running mate, Kwankwaso, and the NDC candidate for Delta North Senatorial District, Victor Ochei, were smashed during the attack. Footages from the scene also showed a counter-mob assaulting some of the alleged attackers apprehended during the melee. Reacting, Ochei called on Governor Sheriff Oborevwori to order immediate investigation into the incident and ensure that those responsible were arrested and prosecuted. Ochei, former Speaker, Delta State House of Assembly, described the attack as unacceptable, accusing the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of resorting to intimidation instead of issue-based political engagement. “I see no reason why the ruling party should descend so low as to mobilise people to attack the opposition. This is condemnable and unacceptable. “If you are doing well as a party, come out and tell the people what you have achieved to merit re-election instead of resorting to intimidation,” Ochei said. He alleged that more than 30 campaign buses were destroyed by suspected attackers allegedly led by commercial tricycle operators under the supervision of an alleged task force official in charge of commercial tricycles in the state. Ochei urged Oborevwori to call APC members to order, warning that Delta should not be turned into a theatre of political violence. “Delta State should not be turned into a theatre of bloodshed,” he said. Also speaking, Delta State Coordinator of the Obi-Kwankwaso Movement (OK Movement) and one of the organisers of the march, Favour Emerue, said the gathering was peaceful until suspected hoodlums disrupted it. He alleged that some participants sustained injuries and were receiving medical attention in hospitals. “This is not the democracy we fought for. Nigerians are ready to defend their votes in 2027 to ensure that the country works. No Deltan should lose his or her life because of an election,” Emerue said. He warned that the governor would be held responsible if any resident lost their life to political violence, while calling on security agencies to investigate and prosecute those culpable. Emerue disclosed that the organisers had notified the police and met with the Commissioner of Police ahead of the march. item.title: Rivers crisis: You’ll not regret choosing peace, Tinubu assures Fubara
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde President Bola Tinubu has assured Rivers State Governor, Siminalayi Fubara, that he would not regret his decision to embrace peace and respect the intervention of political elders in resolving the crisis that rocked the state. Tinubu gave the assurance on Saturday while addressing supporters at the All Progressives Congress, APC, 2027 presidential campaign rally in Port Harcourt. He said, “To me, I intervened on your behalf. Similarly, to Fubara, Your Excellency, the host governor of today, I want to thank you specifically for maturity, understanding, respect for the wisdom of elders. “When we intervened, you respected our position. You maintained peace. You are a committed democrat, Fubara. You will not regret what you have done as long as all of us are alive,” Tinubu said. The political crisis, which erupted in October 2023, followed a breakdown in relations between Fubara and his predecessor, now Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, over control of the state’s political structure. The crisis escalated in March 2025 when Tinubu declared a state of emergency in the state , suspending Fubara, his deputy, Ngozi Odu, and members of the House of Assembly for six months. Fubara returned to office in September 2025 following the expiration of the emergency rule. However, political tensions resurfaced, with lawmakers initiating another impeachment process against him and his deputy in January 2026. Efforts to reconcile the feuding camps gained momentum in June 2025 when Tinubu convened a meeting involving Fubara, Wike and members of the Rivers State House of Assembly at the Presidential Villa in Abuja. More recently, in October , Fubara and Wike held another reconciliation meeting in Port Harcourt alongside their supporters, in what was seen as an effort to consolidate the rapprochement between the two political camps. item.title: Hunger: Tinubu tackles Atiku, asks how he built university as VP
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde President Bola Tinubu has hit back at former Vice President Atiku Abubakar and others criticising his administration over hardship and hunger, accusing them of contributing to the problems he inherited. Tinubu spoke on Saturday at the Rainbow Coalition presidential campaign rally held at the Adokiye Amiesimaka Stadium in Port Harcourt, Rivers State. Responding to those raising concerns about hunger, Tinubu said his administration was working to address the problems left behind by previous governments. “Those people talking of hunger, I’m cleaning the mess they created. Atiku was one of them,” Tinubu said. He then questioned how Atiku, who served as vice president and was involved in economic affairs during the administration of former President Olusegun Obasanjo, was able to establish a university while in office. “Ask him how he built a university while in office as vice president in charge of our economy. Who built the university for him? It’s your money. It’s your effort,” he said. He further questioned Atiku’s moral standing to criticise his administration, describing him as a man lacking the integrity and ethical standards required for public office. Tinubu also expressed appreciation to Rivers residents for the support they gave him during the 2023 presidential election, saying their backing contributed to his emergence as president. “Thank you for the last election. In 2022, 2023, I looked very hopeless, but you trooped out to support me and gave me the mandate,” Tinubu said. “I’m seeking a second term because you believe in me and that I care for you,” he said. item.title: Tinubu: Yari sets 2.3m votes target for Rivers APC
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Director General of the All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council APC-PCC, Sen. Abdulaziz Yari, on Saturday set a target of 2.3 million votes for President Bola Tinubu in Rivers state in the January 16 election. Speaking at the APC presidential campaign rally in Port Harcourt, Yari said the party would mobilize its supporters to achieve the feat. “The message here, we are looking for at least nothing less than 2.3 million votes,” he said. He asked the crowd to raise their hands if they were ready to support the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, to deliver Tinubu at that figure. Yari said the figure was within reach, citing voter data he obtained from the coalition’s leaders in the state. “Out of 3.3 million voters registered and about 2.8 million PVCs collected, we should be aiming at nothing less than 2.3 million,” he said. He told the President that Rivers was one of the states from which the party expected “nothing less than 80 percent, by God’s grace.” Yari also took aim at the opposition, saying those seeking power had themselves been in government without achieving anything tangible. “From Atiku, to Peter Obi, to Amaechi, down to vice president Atiku Abubakar. He was elected as a governor before becoming a vice president,” he said. The Senate President, Godswill Akpabio, said Rivers was the only state in the South-South that Tinubu won convincingly in 2023, and that the state was ready to repeat the feat. He equally added that under Tinubu, Nigeria now gets more revenue from taxation than from crude oil. National Chairman of the APC, Nentawe Yilwatda, described the Tinubu-Shettima ticket as “the best for now in Nigeria.” “Here, we have the numbers. Here, we have the voters,” he said of Rivers. Senator Magnus Abe, who spoke on behalf of Rivers stakeholders, defended the Rainbow Coalition, whose members, he said, have diverse interests but “whose main interest is to return the president to power.” Abe said he was surprised to hear some party members talking down on the coalition. item.title: Why I ditched Atiku – Okowa
item.description: Former Delta State Governor and 2023 running mate to Atiku Abubakar, Senator Ifeanyi Okowa, has explained why he is now supporting President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid. Speaking on Saturday at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Port Harcourt, Rivers State, Okowa said he had “seen the light.” “I have seen the light. Today, we are on the right track because the president is laying a solid foundation,” he declared. Okowa warned against any return of the fuel subsidy, stating that those who previously destroyed Nigeria’s foundation through the subsidy regime must not be allowed to “destroy the future of our children.” At the same rally, Director General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdulaziz Yari, set a target of 2.3 million votes for Tinubu in Rivers State in the January 16 election. He said the figure was achievable, noting that about 2.8 million Permanent Voter Cards had been collected out of 3.3 million registered voters in the state. Yari asked supporters to back Federal Capital Territory Minister Nyesom Wike in delivering the votes and described Rivers as a state from which the party expected “nothing less than 80 percent.” Senate President Godswill Akpabio noted that Rivers was the only South-South state Tinubu won convincingly in 2023 and expressed confidence that the feat would be repeated. He also claimed that under Tinubu, Nigeria now generates more revenue from taxation than from crude oil. APC National Chairman Nentawe Yilwatda described the Tinubu-Shettima ticket as “the best for now in Nigeria,” while Senator Magnus Abe defended the Rainbow Coalition in the state, saying its main interest was to return the president to power. Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi, disappointed by his team’s second-half showing, refused to be drawn on the incident, which was not reviewed on the pitchside monitor by referee John Brooks. “In the first situation of Mathys Tel I didn’t see, I can’t say nothing,” he told TNT Sports after the 1-0 defeat. He added: “I have big confidence in the referee. Nothing changes if he goes to watch the clip or not. I think there was the VAR and if they didn’t take the right decision, I don’t know, but we have confidence.” Defeat is a bitter blow for Spurs, who arrived at Elland Road in buoyant mood after recovering from a shocking start to the season. Leeds manager Daniel Farke said his team, who had been winless in five league games, had shown “great spirit, great commitment, great unity”. Elsewhere, Jacob Murphy put Newcastle on course for a much-needed win with a spectacular strike in the 80th minute at Craven Cottage but substitute Rodrigo Muniz levelled just three minutes later to earn a 1-1 draw. item.title: Tinubu to Nigerian youths: Your future depends on 2027 election
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has urged Nigerian youths to collect their Permanent Voter Cards and participate actively in the 2027 general elections, saying the outcome of the poll will have a direct bearing on their future. Tinubu made the call on Saturday at the Rainbow Coalition presidential campaign rally held at the Adokiye Amiesimaka Stadium in Port Harcourt, Rivers State. Addressing the youths at the rally, the president said the election should not be viewed as being about his personal ambition but about determining the future of the younger generation. “To the youth of Nigeria, I’m looking at you. This election is about you. It’s not about me. Your future depends on this election,” he said. Tinubu urged Nigerians who were yet to collect their PVCs to do so, describing the voter card as the means through which citizens could determine the country’s leadership. “It is left for you to use the weapon you have. And that weapon is the PVC. If you have not collected yours, please go ahead and collect it. Please. I beg you. “I take God, beg you,” he said. The president also identified economic development as a key tool for young Nigerians to overcome poverty, saying his administration was working to improve the economy and ensure that prosperity was widely shared. He said previous administrations had left behind unpaid pensions and gratuities running into billions and trillions of naira, adding that his government was clearing the outstanding obligations. “The people that governed before left unpaid pensions and gratuity in billions and trillions of naira. That is being cleared. So that every family is included. We are sharing prosperity already,” Tinubu said. He listed retired professionals, including engineers, welders, and teachers, among those benefiting from the payments. “A retired engineer is receiving their gratuity right now. A retired welder is receiving the pension right now. A retired teacher is receiving the pension right now,” he added. item.title: Argentina FA to appeal World Cup final sanctions to CAS
item.description: Argentina’s football association (AFA) announced on Saturday it had appealed to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) against the sanctions FIFA imposed on it over World Cup final incidents. Midfielder Leandro Paredes was the hardest hit with a 10-game ban and $90,000 fine for his role in clashes with Spain players. He grabbed Eric Garcia by the throat and wrestled Gavi to the ground while holding his substitute’s bib, which led to an escalation in the incidents on the field after the final that Spain won 1-0 at the MetLife Stadium in New Jersey on July 19. The AFA was fined $321,000 for breaches of FIFA’s disciplinary code relating to using a sports event for making demonstrations of a non-sporting nature, team misconduct, and discriminatory chants and gestures by its supporters. Nahuel Molina and Thiago Almada were also hit with bans and fines, as was Roberto Ayala, a member of Argentina’s coaching team. In a statement, AFA said FIFA’s appeals body had rejected their complaint against the sanctions handed out to Paredes and the association, but had reduced Molina’s punishment from a seven-match ban and $90,000 fine to four games and $60,000. AFA also stated it would now take its appeals against its own and Paredes’s sanctions to CAS. The post Argentina FA to appeal World Cup final sanctions to CAS appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Re-election: Tinubu lists economy, education, healthcare as priorities
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has pledged to give priority attention to education, economic recovery, healthcare and citizens’ welfare if given another mandate in 2027. Tinubu made the pledge at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Port Harcourt on Saturday. Speaking at the rally co-organised by the Rainbow Coalition led by Chief Nyesom Wike, the Minister, Federal Capital Territory, Tinubu also said that youth development would be given deserved attention. The president urged Rivers people to use their Permanent Voter Cards wisely to achieve a better and more progressive Nigeria. He expressed his administration’s commitment to promote the welfare of retirees through enhanced and prompt payment of pensions and gratuities. He commended Wike and the people of Rivers for massively expressing their resolve to support his re-election bid. The president thanked Wike for his commitment to reconciliation and peace-building during the political crisis that rocked the state. Tinubu also commended Gov. Siminalayi Fubara for being a peaceful leader and lover of his state, saying, “The governor will never regret his commitment to restoring peace in the state.” “I sincerely appreciate Wike, Fubara, APC members and the Rainbow Coalition Campaign Council for their support,” he said. Earlier, Wike assured the president that Rivers residents would massively support his re-election bid. He said that Tinubu had demonstrated huge support to the state by appointing no fewer than 47 Rivers people into strategic positions at the national level. “We cannot take the president’s support for granted. Rivers people will vote massively for the president in the 2027 presidential election,” he said. Also speaking, Fubara said that Rivers would deliver no fewer than three million votes in support of the president’s re-election bid. “We shall continue to work together to ensure that the president wins the election; that is our promise,” he said. He thanked the campaign team for providing an opportunity for Rivers people to demonstrate their political strength and support for the president. Fubara thanked Tinubu for his commitment to the development of the Niger Delta Region through critical infrastructure projects, especially the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that while in the state, Tinubu inaugurated the Bonny-Bodo Road project. He also presented the APC governorship flag to the party’s candidate in Rivers, Mr Kingsley Chinda. item.title: Hope you’ll visit 33 other states after Akwa Ibom ‘sleep’ – Obi tells Tinubu
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has challenged President Bola Tinubu to extend his visits to the remaining 33 states of the federation after spending a night in Akwa Ibom State. Obi made the call in a post on X on Saturday, following Tinubu’s visit to Akwa Ibom, where the president said his overnight stay would be a “second term presidential sleep” ahead of the 2027 election. Obi congratulated Tinubu on spending a night in a state outside Lagos and Abuja, urging the president to use such visits to engage directly with Nigerians and explain the impact of his administration. He said he hoped the Akwa Ibom visit would encourage Tinubu to travel to the other 33 states, spend time with the people and account for the resources accruing to the Federal Government. “I sincerely hope this visit will inspire you to travel to the remaining 33 states of the federation, spend time with the people and, more importantly, explain what your administration has done with the ₦15.8 trillion saved from the removal of fuel subsidy, the over $100 billion you have borrowed, the increased revenues accruing to the government from taxing Nigerians, and the additional government revenues which your administration celebrated last year as having surpassed its target,” Obi said. The former Anambra State governor also demanded explanations on the impact of government policies on poverty, education, healthcare and electricity. He asked the President to state how many Nigerians had been lifted out of poverty, how many out-of-school children had returned to school and how many functional primary healthcare centres had been built. Obi also questioned the improvement in electricity supply, recalling Tinubu’s earlier promise that Nigerians should not vote for him if his administration failed to fix the power sector. On insecurity, he said Nigerians deserved an explanation of what the government had done to secure the country, which he noted still ranks among the world’s most terrorised countries. “Mr President, Nigerians deserve answers. They deserve to know what has been done with the resources entrusted to your government,” Obi said. He added that the New Nigeria he seeks to build would be founded on accountability, transparency and the measurable impact of public resources on citizens. Tinubu had on Friday told supporters at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium, Uyo, that he would spend the night in Akwa Ibom, describing it as a “second term presidential sleep” and expressing confidence in securing re-election in 2027. item.title: PVC Is Your Weapon Against Poverty, Tinubu Tells Supporters In Rivers

If you have not collected yours, please go ahead and collect it. Please, I beg you, I take God beg. The weapon you have against poverty is to elect progressive development of our economy. That is what I am pursuing,” Tinubu said. ﻿ Addressing Nigerian youths, the President said the outcome of the 2027 elections would have a direct impact on their future, urging them to take the exercise seriously. “To the youths of Nigeria, I am looking at you. item.title: Ebola: DRC records 10,668 cases, 5,198 deaths — WHO
item.description: The disease, Bundibugyo virus disease, with transmission continuing across eight provinces, the World Health Organization (WHO) says. The WHO said in a statement on Saturday that the figure recorded was as of Nov. 3, representing a case fatality ratio of 48.7 percent. It said the outbreak had spread geographically, with active transmission ongoing in 51 of the 67 affected health zones across eight provinces. According to WHO, although some areas have recorded a slight decline in cases, sustained and high-level transmission continues across DRC. The organization said 512 deaths had been reported since Oct. 21, comprising 335 deaths in communities and 177 in treatment centers. It expressed concern over the high number of community deaths, particularly among young children, attributing the trend to challenges in early detection and timely access to appropriate healthcare. “No new cases had been reported in Kenya and Nigeria since its previous Disease Outbreak News published on Oct. 23. “However, there is the need for sustained regional preparedness, including cross-border surveillance, monitoring at points of entry, early case detection, and coordinated response measures,” it said. The organization also disclosed that Switzerland and the United Kingdom had medically evacuated confirmed cases involving their citizens, although no new country had reported cases since the previous update. WHO advised against imposing travel or trade restrictions on countries experiencing or responding to the outbreak, based on currently available information. item.title: Poor power supply threatens students’ academic activities, NAUS warns
item.description: The National Association of University Students has called on the Federal Ministry of Power to urgently address persistent electricity shortages in university campuses and student-populated communities, warning that the situation is undermining academic activities, students’ businesses and personal security. The association, which represents more than 21.2 million undergraduate and postgraduate students in Nigeria and the diaspora, said unreliable electricity was making it increasingly difficult for students to study, conduct research, attend virtual lectures and meet academic deadlines. The National President of NAUS, Comrade Dr Meshach Anthony Nwankwo, made the appeal in a statement made available to journalists in Abuja on Saturday. Nwankwo urged the Minister of Power, Chief Joseph Olasunkanmi Tegbe, to prioritise sustainable electricity supply to university communities, stressing that access to reliable power was essential to improving the quality of higher education. He acknowledged President Bola Tinubu’s efforts to expand access to education and strengthen student support systems. He also commended the Minister of Education, Dr Maruf Olatunji Alausa, for translating the President’s educational agenda into policies and programmes. The NAUS president, however, insisted that educational reforms would have limited impact without a reliable electricity supply to support teaching, learning and research. According to him, electricity is no longer a luxury for university students but a necessity for academic survival. “For the average Nigerian university student, electricity goes beyond having light in a room. It determines whether they can charge their phones and laptops, access lecture materials, conduct research, complete assignments, attend virtual classes and prepare adequately for examinations,” he said. He expressed concern that students were sometimes forced to leave their residences in search of places to charge their electronic devices, exposing them to avoidable security risks. He particularly raised concerns about the vulnerability of female students who might be compelled to seek charging facilities in unfamiliar or unsecured environments. “These are not experiences that should form part of the burden of acquiring a university education,” he said. Nwankwo noted that the electricity crisis also affected lecturers and other academic personnel living within university communities, making it difficult for them to prepare lectures, conduct research and discharge their professional responsibilities. He said the consequences of poor electricity supply extended beyond students’ academic performance, weakening the entire university ecosystem. The association therefore appealed to the Ministry of Power to consider targeted interventions that would guarantee sustainable electricity supply across university campuses and surrounding communities. item.title: Oyo’ll no longer depend on oil, raw materials for economic prosperity – Makinde
item.description: …state targets global market for arts, crafts By Adeola Badru The Oyo State Government has declared its determination to move beyond dependence on conventional sources of revenue by harnessing the economic potential of arts, crafts, cultural festivals, and tourism to generate foreign exchange, attract international investments, and create employment opportunities. The government said it was working to transform Nigeria’s rich cultural heritage into commercially viable products for the global export market, positioning the creative economy as a major driver of economic growth and sustainable development. The initiative, which sought to unlock the enormous economic value of indigenous artistic expressions, traditional knowledge, and cultural assets, will be driven through the Oyo State Business Forum 2026, with the theme “Investment and Export Promotion of Arts and Crafts Business in Oyo State.” The forum is expected to bring together investors, artists, craftsmen, exporters, policymakers, and development partners to explore investment opportunities, strengthen export capacity, and expand the international market for Nigerian arts and crafts. Speaking at a press briefing to announce the forum, the Commissioner for Culture and Tourism, Dr. Wasiu Olatubosun, said the administration of Governor Seyi Makinde was deliberately repositioning culture beyond its traditional function as a custodian of heritage to become a productive economic sector capable of generating wealth, attracting investments, and contributing meaningfully to national development. Olatubosun, who spoke at the briefing organized in collaboration with the Oyo State Investment and Public-Private Partnership Agency (OYSIPA) at the state Secretariat, Ibadan, described Nigeria’s cultural wealth as an enormous but largely untapped economic resource that could compete favorably in the international marketplace. He maintained that traditional festivals, indigenous knowledge, artistic expressions, and locally produced crafts possessed considerable commercial value and could become major export commodities if properly researched, documented, developed, and marketed. According to him, the state government is also repositioning its cultural festivals from routine annual celebrations into internationally competitive tourism and entertainment products capable of attracting foreign visitors, investors, and members of the African diaspora. He identified the recent inscription of the Sango Festival on UNESCO’s Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity as a major boost to Oyo State’s international cultural standing and an opportunity to attract greater global attention. The commissioner explained that the recognition had taken the annual festival in Oyo Town beyond its traditional geographical and cultural boundaries, making it an increasingly attractive destination for international tourists, cultural enthusiasts, and media organizations from Africa, Europe, and the Americas.

item.title: Tinubu-Shettima ticket most formidable in Nigeria’s history, says APC chair
item.description: The National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Nentawe Yilwatda, has described the presidential ticket of President Bola Tinubu and Vice-President Kashim Shettima as the most formidable in Nigeria’s political history, urging Nigerians to support their re-election in 2027. Yilwatda said Tinubu deserved another term to consolidate the economic reforms and infrastructure projects initiated by his administration. He made the remarks on Saturday at the Rainbow Coalition Presidential Campaign Rally held at the Adokiye Amiesimaka Stadium in Port Harcourt, Rivers State. In a statement issued by his Special Adviser on Media and Information Strategy, Abimbola Tooki, the APC chairman said the Tinubu-Shettima ticket combined political experience, courage and leadership capacity needed to address the country’s challenges. “The most formidable presidential ticket we have ever produced in Nigeria is the Tinubu-Shettima ticket. We have a candidate in President Bola Ahmed Tinubu who is fearless, courageous and determined to confront the challenges of our country. He has demonstrated the capacity to take difficult decisions in the national interest, and he has remained resolute in pursuing the transformation of Nigeria,” he said. Yilwatda defended the administration’s economic policies, including the removal of the petrol subsidy and the unification of the foreign exchange market, describing them as necessary steps towards rebuilding the economy and strengthening public finances. Although he acknowledged that the reforms had created difficulties for households and businesses, he said the government was working to cushion their effects through economic stabilisation measures, social interventions and infrastructure investments. The APC chairman also praised Tinubu’s infrastructure programme, particularly major highway projects, which he said would improve connectivity, facilitate trade and create economic opportunities. “We have a President who understands that development cannot happen without infrastructure. He has initiated an ambitious infrastructure revolution through major highway projects that will connect different parts of Nigeria, open up economic corridors, facilitate the movement of goods and services and create new opportunities for our people,” Yilwatda said. He urged Nigerians to support the continuation of the administration’s policies, arguing that a second term would allow Tinubu to consolidate the reforms and deliver their expected benefits.
